text:
dana: Heads-up — after the kv-blockpack patch landed on main I see a consistent tail-latency bump for mixed GQA/MQA traffic. Numbers from canary: p95 increased ~10%, p99 ~18%. :thinking:

mike: on which model / config? can you paste the exact run?

dana: repro is on rdl-gpt-13b-8k, MQA enabled with 4-bit quant, kv layout changed to stride-aware blockpacking (new allocator). Canary run: `wrk` style gen with 200 concurrent streams, seq_len dist ~ [16,64,512]. Baseline (old layout): p95 92ms, p99 210ms. After blockpack: p95 102ms, p99 248ms.

julia: hmm. is this more visible on long sequences?

dana: it's amplified when >384 tokens. For short convo bursts p50 unchanged. My hypothesis: the allocator increases page-fragmentation which breaks the paged-attn kernel prefetch pattern, causing more small kernel hops and extra kernel selection churn.

sam: any kernel selector logs? we added extra fallback path recently.

dana: attached profiler snippet (sanitized):

```
# timeline (canary run)
KV-PageMap::lookup  ->  avg 0.8us (short seq)
KV-PageMap::lookup  ->  avg 2.7us (long seq)
kernel_picker.select -> 1.2us -> chosen: paged-attn-blocksz=256 (old) / paged-attn-blocksz=128 (new)
kernel_dispatch     -> 4-9us extra per token for long seqs
```

mike: do we change block size to 128 globally in that PR? thought we used heuristic: chunk by model shard density + seqlen histogram.

dana: PR moved to a stride-aware packing and default blocksz=128 when fragmentation ratio > 0.3. That heuristic might be too aggressive for MQA workloads where KV stripes are interleaved.

perf-bot: regression-detect: commit 9f3a2d3 increased p99 by +18% for rdl-gpt-13b-8k on canary.

julia: quick experiment idea: try forcing blocksz=256 for MQA/GQA mixed route and see if selector picks fewer kernel transitions. can we flip flag at runtime?

mike: yes `RUNTIME_FLAG=kv.blockpack.force_blocksz=256` on canary nodepool. trying now.

infra-bot: deploy started to canary pool: pool-id cny-4, change: set kv.blockpack.force_blocksz=256.

mike: preliminary after flip: p95 back to ~93ms, p99 215ms. still slightly above baseline but much closer.

dana: OK that narrows it to blocksize heuristic. I also see selector churn logs where kernel_picker toggles between gqa-optimized path and mqa-interleaved path within same request for long sequences — extra context switch cost.

sam: could be because of mixed-precision quant paths differing kernel codegen for 4-bit. If the allocator changes physical layout between KV lookups, the kernel cache key changes and we recompiling/rehashing.

julia: actionable plan: 1) revert aggressive fragmentation threshold, 2) add seqlen-gated rule: if >25% requests in window >256 tokens, prefer larger blocksz, 3) add a fast-path sticky kernel selection per request id to avoid mid-request swaps.

mike: agree. also add more detailed kernel_picker metrics: transitions/request, distinct_kernels/request. we currently only emit chosen kernel per RPC.

dana: I'll open a tiny PR with telemetry + the runtime flag default to 256 for MQA routes. Would like someone to review the sticky-selection patch — it's a little invasive in the dispatcher. @mike @julia

mike: I'll take sticky-selection. will prototype with a per-rpc sticky bit in the req context. two caveats: memory of sticky binding must be tiny and must expire at end of req to avoid cross-request bias.

julia: I'll handle telemetry and the heuristic rollback. add unit tests that synthetic workloads with mixed seqlen produce no more than 3 kernel transitions per request on average.

perf-bot: benchmark job queued: job/kv-blockpack-revert-telemetry-176500 -> estimated 45m.

dana: thanks — also adding a quick reproduction script to `eng/runtime/bench` so other folks can run the mixed GQA/MQA profile locally: `scripts/mqa_gqa_mixed_warmup.sh`.

sam: ping if you want me to run GPU profiler (nsys) on a node — I can capture the kernel dispatch timeline.

mike: will follow up with small patch in a few hours. thx everyone :thumbsup:

julia: leaving notes here: possible root causes list: [1] blocksize downshift -> more kernel hops, [2] physical KV fragmentation -> prefetch miss, [3] kernel cache key variance due to layout -> recompiles, [4] runtime selector threshold oscillation. We'll iterate. :eyes:
